structured.approach: I followed the data-engineering-steps skill for DE-06. First I got receipts for both contracted inputs through context_get: feat.data_model_change at 379f011 and org.customer_mappings at a6b3e2a. I searched shared memory for mapping decisions and found none beyond D-2026-031 and D-2026-044. I read the ap_pipeline code and schedule.json from the step's tool view. Then I checked the latest customer contract (feed v3 columns, the paid_date -> Invoice.paid_date mapping and the schedule) against the Data Model change, one field at a time. I wrote feat.mappings with these parts: the customer contract compared with the model, the feed-row to Invoice mapping, ordered transformation steps, the derived Invoice to Delay-history mapping, a schedule comparison, mapping validation cases on synthetic rows, and open questions. This step is a mapping step, so I changed no code; the coding step implements it. I ran CI once on the unchanged repo and it passed, but I cite no CI figures because this step has no tool:ci view. I did not use any connector, because the inputs held every fact I needed.
tools_used: Bash (baseline CI run, no code changed)

claims.text: The latest customer contract for feed v3 lists the columns invoice_id, vendor, due_date, amount, paid and paid_date. paid_date is optional, an ISO date, and empty when unpaid. The contract maps paid_date to Invoice.paid_date.
The customer mapping agrees with the Data Model change. paid_date is a nullable date on Invoice. Blank or missing gives None. A non-blank invalid value rejects the row with reason paid_date.
The mappings for invoice_id, vendor, due_date, amount and paid are unchanged from today's transform.to_model. amount stays Decimal, never float.
paid_date is mapped only after the existing fields map successfully, so an existing reject reason such as ValueError wins over paid_date (DD-6).
The data-quality report needs no code change, because reject_reasons is the sorted set of rejected reasons, so paid_date shows up there on its own.
The Delay history maps vendor to a list of (paid_date - due_date).days. It includes only records that are paid and have a paid_date, keeps feed order, and is held in memory only.
The customer schedule is daily at 02:00 Asia/Kolkata and unchanged. It matches schedule.json (frequency daily, time 02:00, timezone Asia/Kolkata).
The customer contract confirms the column spelling paid_date, which answers the carried open question DMQ-B.
This step changes no code. The tool view shows transform.py without paid_date and no delays.py. TC-1 and TC-2 implement the mapping in a later Data Engineering coding step.
This step read only the contracted inputs, the tool view and synthetic rows. It read no production or source-system data.

open_questions: MQ-A: The customer contract lists 'paid_date', which answers DMQ-B (the column spelling). Can DMQ-B be closed? Interim answer: yes.

MQ-B: The customer contract says paid_date is 'empty when unpaid', but the model keeps an unpaid record that has a valid paid_date (DD-7, interim). Should such a row be rejected or have paid_date cleared instead? Interim answer: keep it; the Delay history ignores it.
MQ-C: The contract gives no effective date for v3. Must v2 and v3 feeds be accepted side by side? Interim answer: yes; the mapping already handles a missing column as None.
structured.summary: I wrote feat.mappings for FEAT-ZD-48600. The latest customer contract (feed v3) adds one mapping, paid_date -> Invoice.paid_date, and it agrees field by field with the DE-05 Data Model change. The five existing column mappings are unchanged. The output covers the ordered transformation steps (paid_date validated last, reject reason paid_date, data-quality report unchanged), the derived Delay-history mapping and synthetic validation cases. The schedule stays daily 02:00 Asia/Kolkata, which matches schedule.json. This step changed no code. There are three non-blocking open questions and no blocking ones.
